minutes.headline: Planning Board declined to endorse an ANR for 932 Flat Hill Road over owner authorization, then approved two stormwater occupancy sign-offs.
minutes.summary: The board heard civics students ask for sidewalks, a BSC Group presentation on reuse options for 925 Massachusetts Ave, and took up several stormwater and ANR matters. It voted not to endorse an ANR for 932 Flat Hill Road at this time because the land being added belongs to a different owner than the applicant. It authorized occupancy sign-offs for 430 Mulpus Road and a temporary one for 321 Sunny Hill Road, both with performance guarantees. The interim land use director also flagged MBTA Communities zoning options, which the board asked to place on the next agenda.

public_comment.topic: Lunenburg High School civics students asked the board to prioritize sidewalks, especially extending the sidewalk on the west side of Massachusetts Avenue, and presented survey data (about 104 student responses).
An engineer gave informal updates: 255 Sunny Hill is still in conservation commission peer review, and 171 Arbor Street is pursuing ZBA filings before returning to the board.
Asked about the board's status on MBTA Communities zoning, cited other towns pushing back or voting no, and raised concerns about unit density and state mandates.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted not to endorse, at this time, an ANR for 932 Flat Hill Road because the land being divided belongs to someone other than the signed applicant.
The board authorized an occupancy sign-off for 430 Mulpus Road (Lot 2), conditioned on a performance guarantee held under a tri-party agreement and a six-month growing-season hold.
The board authorized a temporary occupancy sign-off for 321 Sunny Hill Road, with one guarantee covering both 321 and 317 that is not released until all work is complete.
The interim land use director raised MBTA Communities zoning options, and the board agreed to put them on the next agenda with Regional Planning Agency staff invited.
The board heard Lunenburg High School civics students ask for sidewalks and received a BSC Group presentation on reuse options for 925 Massachusetts Ave.

why_it_matters: Performance guarantees held back until stormwater work is finished and proven over a growing season are how the town keeps drainage and runoff problems from landing on neighbors and on public budgets after a project is occupied.
MBTA Communities zoning is a state-driven requirement that could bring a zoning change vote to residents, and the board is still weighing it against the grants tied to compliance.
The sidewalk request and the 925 Massachusetts Ave reuse options are early input that could shape future capital and master-plan spending.
watch_next: The next Planning Board agenda, which is to include MBTA Communities zoning options with Regional Planning Agency staff invited.
The June 10 meeting, where Graves Engineering's review of the 274 Prospect Street stormwater modification is due and an MRPC representative is to be elected.
